item.title: Top Democrat Opposes Trump’s Planned Sale of Heavy Bombs to Israel
item.description: The administration has options to bypass the objection, but the move highlights a sensitive issue ahead of the midterms.

item.title: Harold Hamm’s Continental Resources Signs Preliminary Oil Deal in Venezuela
item.description: The company, led by one of President Trump’s closest allies in the U.S. oil industry, said it would explore one of Venezuela’s undeveloped oil fields.

item.title: U.S. Probes Iran Link to Cyberattacks on Texas-Bound Energy Tankers
item.description: The vessels were attacked in the Strait of Gibraltar as they made their way to U.S. ports.

item.title: Yemen’s Houthi Rebels Claim Shooting Down Saudi F-15 Jet Fighter
item.description: The claimed downing of the Saudi jet comes as the kingdom is squeezed by the Iran-backed rebels’ advance and attacks targeting its oil industry.

item.title: Debris Found in Yemen Suggests Saudi Arabia Fired Its First Chinese Missile
item.description: The body of what appeared to be a Dongfeng 15 was found in the desert.

item.title: EU Chief Backs Canada’s Push to Become Bloc’s First Associate Member
item.description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen’s comments follow efforts by Canada’s Mark Carney to accelerate his country’s pivot to the bloc.

item.title: What Would Canada’s Associate Membership of the EU Look Like?
item.description: The title is entirely new and significant hurdles remain before it could become Canada’s official status.

item.title: Former Kosovo President Sentenced to 25 Years for War Crimes in Serbia Conflict
item.description: Hashim Thaci was convicted in one of the final verdicts in a series of landmark trials arising from the bloody dissolution of the former Yugoslavia.

item.title: Best High-Yield Savings Accounts for September 2026: Up to 4.50%
item.description: These are the accounts that offer the best interest rates—without burdensome fees, gimmicks or other hassles

item.title: Eurozone Industrial Production Fell at Start of Third Quarter
item.description: The data highlights the uneven nature of the region’s recovery as manufacturers contend with higher energy costs despite signs of improving demand.

item.title: EU Chief Reveals Plans for Curbing Children’s Access to Social Media
item.description: The European Commission’s president revealed details of a plan for a new EU-wide law curbing minors’ access to social networks.

item.title: This English Village Is Threatening to Quit the U.K. Over Planned Asylum Camp
item.description: Piddington, population 350, is up in arms over a proposal to house 1,250 asylum seekers at a former military site.

item.title: The U.S. Is Burning Through Its Supply of Interceptors to Counter Iran’s Attacks
item.description: The U.S. had to expend 70 or more Patriots and Thaads to blunt an attack on Jordan.

item.title: Elon Musk Trains His Political Chaos Machine on the U.K.
item.description: Using his social-media megaphone to roil the waters, Musk is promoting a new anti-immigration party.

item.title: How a Chinese Hacking Firm Tapped AI to Supercharge Cyber-Spying
item.description: Internal company materials illustrate an AI-powered effort to make pilfered foreign government documents digestible for police; targets include Russia, Pakistan.

item.title: Ed Sheeran’s Opening Acts Quit in Solidarity With Pro-Palestinian Performer
item.description: Rapper Macklemore was dropped from the Loop Tour after onstage comments about Gaza.

item.title: AWS Says It Can’t Restore Some Data From Mideast Facilities Struck by Iran
item.description: Amazon’s announcement is the first indication that some data stored exclusively in Bahrain and the U.A.E could be gone forever.

item.title: Oil Prices Rise as Middle East Supply Concerns Persist
item.description: Oil prices rose to four-month highs with the shutdown of Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline and Houthi threats to shipping in the Red Sea keeping the market on edge about supply out of the Middle East.

item.title: Canada Looks to Lure New Investment With Aggressive, Broad Tax Writeoff Terms
item.description: Canada is implementing a tax change tied to the accelerated write off of capital equipment that attempts to move the country toward Prime Minister Mark Carney’s goal of attracting nearly $1 trillion of new investment.

item.title: Russia’s Shadow Fleet Is Sailing in NATO’s Blind Spot: Irish Waters
item.description: A growing number of suspected Russian shadow fleet ships regularly ply waters near Ireland that hold many crucial undersea cables.
